findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS MySQL volume, automated snapshots and any manual snapshots in cleartext, exposing all database contents to anyone who can reach the underlying storage or copy a snapshot.

publicly_accessible = true gives the database a public endpoint reachable from the internet; combined with the default 'admin' master user, static password auth and no encryption, this is a direct exposure of the data tier.

The master user is the predictable default 'admin' and the password comes from a plain Terraform variable, which is persisted unencrypted in state and reused verbatim in EC2 user_data instead of being sourced from Secrets Manager or the managed master password feature.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so the publicly reachable instance depends solely on a long-lived static master password with no centrally revocable, short-lived credential option.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the PHP application (which calls mysqli_connect with no TLS options) and any internet client can authenticate and transfer data to the publicly accessible database in cleartext.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Attached via an instance profile to an internet-facing web server, theft of the instance credentials yields near-total control of storage, compute and databases in the account, including privilege-escalation paths through ec2 actions.

user_data interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into a PHP include file; EC2 user data is retrievable in cleartext from the instance metadata service and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, and is stored unencrypted in Terraform state, leaking the database master credentials.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. An SSRF or application flaw in the deployed PHP page can retrieve credentials for the wildcard-privileged ec2role instance profile.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root volume holding the generated /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc credential file may be left unencrypted at rest.

The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, removing an egress control that would otherwise constrain data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database tier.
